subject: Custody control matrix & DPA trigger: transient-transfer handling and escalation
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@medtrax.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedTrax Legal <legal@medtrax.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 13:22:00 -0400
Subject: Custody assurance — question on transient cross-hop triggers and on-call escalation

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal asked me to consolidate a couple of operational clarifications so they can sign the DPA annex. Their two sticking points are below — can you confirm whether Redwood can either: (a) commit to explicit trigger windows in the DPA annex, or (b) accept an operational control matrix + escalation SLA that sits outside the core DPA?

1) Transient cross-hop processing: our compliance team understands that in failover or burst scenarios some processing may briefly occur outside the primary custody territory (they call this a "transient-sync"). They want: a maximum duration per incident, notification timing to customer security contacts, and a signed set of controls that limit what data is allowed to be processed during the transient window.

2) Subprocessor activation triggers: they want a deterministic mechanism that tells us when and how Redwood will invoke a subprocessor in another region (e.g., monitoring, analytics, or fallback compute). Specifically — a mapping between trigger type, expected time-to-activate, and the data categories allowed to cross for that activation.

I attached a short list of questions from their counsel (MedTrax_DPA_question_list.docx). Could you loop in the right folks? If you have a custody-control matrix or a sample annex we can review quickly, that would help speed legal sign-off.

Appreciate it —
Priya
Data Protection Lead
MedTrax Inc.

Attachments: MedTrax_DPA_question_list.docx

Hi Priya — thanks for consolidating this. Copying Marissa (legal) and Jordan (SRE/product ops) to propose an operational approach. Jordan — can you attach the latest custody control matrix (we keep it as an ops workbook) and confirm the default transient window we use for burst failovers? For clarity for MedTrax, their ask is: a) an explicit maximum duration per incident and b) a notification SLA once those hops occur. Our proposed defaults are in the matrix but we can make them DPA-level if necessary.

Priya — proposed next steps:

- If required, we can create a short, signed addendum that references the matrix and is attached to the DPA.

Would Friday EOD (May 21) for a first-pass be acceptable?

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custody assurance — question on transient cross-hop triggers and on-call escalation

Priya / team — attaching the operational artefacts you requested. Short summary inline, then attachments: redwood_custody_control_matrix_v1.xlsx (tabbed by trigger type), and a draft DPA annex PDF that contains a short "transient-transfer" clause we typically propose. Key points: 

- Trigger taxonomy: Scheduled maintenance (planned), Unscheduled failing-of-primary-availability (failover), Load-burst overflow (auto-scale), and Emergency operator access (break-glass).
- For each trigger we list: allowed data categories (pseudonymized metadata only; no full PII for burst overflow by default), maximum continuous processing window (default 72 hours for failover with operational mitigations; 4 hours for burst auto-scale), and notification windows (initial alert within 60 minutes; full incident report within 72 hours).
- Subprocessor map: we disclose the roster and classify activations as either automatic (e.g., autoscaling to regional pool) or manual (ops-triggered). Automatic activations for autoscale only process low-sensitivity artifacts; analytics/monitoring subprocessors only receive telemetry and aggregated metrics unless specifically enabled in an SLA-bound configuration.

Marissa — two optional wording approaches included in the PDF: (A) explicit DPA annex that lists the default windows and data categories (binds us contractually), or (B) a DPA clause referencing an operational custody control matrix maintained by Redwood with a notification-and-review commitment. We prefer (B) for agility but can accept (A) if MedTrax needs absolute contractual windows.

Attached: redwood_custody_control_matrix_v1.xlsx, DPA_annex-transient-sync-draft.pdf

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Product Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_custody_control_matrix_v1.xlsx; DPA_annex-transient-sync-draft.pdf

Subject: Re: Custody assurance — question on transient cross-hop triggers and on-call escalation

Jordan / Jonas — thank you, this is really helpful and addresses most of our counsel's concerns. A few follow-ups from Legal after reviewing the matrix and draft annex: 

1) The 72-hour default for failover: Legal wants that reduced to 48 hours for high-sensitivity datasets and wants a mandatory mitigation checklist (e.g., encryption-in-transit enforced, KV-cache scrub) that must be executed prior to the 48-72h window being exhausted. Could Redwood accept a tiered maximum (48h for high-sensitivity, 72h default) and include the mitigation checklist as an attachment to the annex?

2) Subprocessor activation: they want the clause to require written notice to the DPO for any manual activation affecting personal data beyond telemetry, with a 24-hour advance notice where feasible. Can Redwood add that to the manual activation path?

3) Certification ask: Legal is also asking for one example incident report (redacted) showing how you notified and documented a transient cross-hop in the prior 12 months. If you can share a sanitized sample, that will get them comfortable.

If you can update the annex to reflect (1) tiered windows + mitigation checklist, and (2) manual-activation notification language, we can aim to route this through counsel next week. Thank you —

Priya Sharma
Data Protection Lead
MedTrax Inc.

Attachments: none
